subject: RE: Brightlane renewal — escalation for concession approval
messages:
From: Sarah Lind <sarah.lind@brightlane.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: Renewal terms — need help to keep contract

Jordan / Marissa,

Thanks for the patient conversations this week. As we discussed on the call, Brightlane is facing a Q2 budget reforecast driven by reduced payer reimbursements. We value the product and the reliability your team has delivered, but procurement has mandated material cuts in SaaS spend.

At renewal (current term ends 2026-04-15) our options are: 1) push to a competitor with a lower unit cost, or 2) keep Redwood but require a combination of a one-time credit and a longer fixed term with a lower ARR.

Specifically, procurement requested the following to recommend renewal to the CFO: a 15% one-time discount applied to the first invoice of the renewed term OR a 3-month credit (applied as invoice credit) plus a 12-month term reset, and an add-on SLA to reach 99.9% for production endpoints. They also asked that we commit to the same pricing for the first 12 months of the renewed term.

We are asking Redwood for a final, executable concession package by EOD Wednesday so procurement can include it in the renewal packet. If we can’t get something close, they will proceed with the alternative.

Attached: renewal_summary (but I will send the formal PO once approved).

—Sarah
Sarah Lind
Head of Platform Operations
Brightlane Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lind <sarah.lind@brightlane.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Urgent: Renewal terms — need help to keep contract

Sarah — thanks for the transparency and the note. I’m escalating this to the deal desk and leadership for a quick decision.

Short summary of what you asked for (so we’re aligned): 15% one-time discount OR 3-month credit + 12-month reset, and a 99.9% SLA add-on. We’ll come back with a proposal that balances revenue impact and retention risk.

Laura / Marissa: looping you in to request an exception approval. I’ll compile an impact summary and a clean amendment to circulate.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Brightlane renewal — deal desk recommendation + attachments

Team — I ran quick numbers with finance (sketch attached). Brightlane is a mid-sized payer/partner with healthy usage growth (70% token growth last year) but the customer is price sensitive for the next 12 months. They are strategic in our health vertical, so retention has platform value.

Options we can propose (ranked):
- Option A (recommended): 10% one-time invoice credit + one-time 60-day service credit (applied as invoice credit) + 12-month term reset. Require customer to sign a 12-month renewal at standard MRR thereafter.
- Option B: 15% up-front discount OR 3-month credit + 12-month reset (as requested) — this is higher revenue impact; needs Exec approval (Evelyn).
- Option C: Keep price, offer 1 month free + health check/whiteglove onboarding to lock renewal (lower revenue hit but less likely to meet procurement ask).

Attachments: Brightlane_Renewal_Summary_v3.pdf (usage and ARR impact), proposed_amendment_redline.docx (template amendment with SLA language).

Vivek — we need your sign-off for any concession >10% or credits >60 days. If you can greenlight Option A today, Jordan should propose it as the default and ask Brightlane to accept by Friday. If Brightlane pushes for Option B we need Evelyn to authorize the incremental delta.

Laura Bennett
VP Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Brightlane renewal — deal desk recommendation + attachments

Laura / Jordan — I reviewed the attachment and P&L impact. Recommendation: approve Option A (10% + 60-day credit + 12-month reset) as an exception that Revenue Ops can sign below a 12% threshold. For anything that effectively reduces recognized ARR by >12% in year-1 (Option B as-is would), we need written exec approval.

Rationale: customer lifetime value and the health vertical strategic multiplier make a modest concession acceptable. But we should not set a precedent for 15% standard discounts. If the customer insists on Option B, escalate to Evelyn for final sign-off and legal for SLA wording.

Action items: Jordan — present Option A as the primary offer and keep Option B as an approval-level alternate. Marissa — please prep the amendment redline with explicit SLA SLOs and failure credits.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lind <sarah.lind@brightlane.com>, procurement@brightlane.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Brightlane renewal — proposed concession package (pending exec sign-off)

Sarah — per our internal review, here is our primary offer to present internally:

Option A (preferred / approved by RevOps): 10% one-time invoice credit applied to the first renewal invoice + one-time 60-day service credit (applied as invoice credit) + 12-month term reset. We will include an SLA addendum targeting 99.9% uptime for production endpoints; final SLA language to be reviewed by legal.

If procurement requires the alternative (15% or 3-month credit), we will escalate for executive approval; that path may take 48–72 hours. Please let me know if Option A would be acceptable for the CFO packet; if so I’ll circulate the clean amendment for signature and route to DocuSign.

Attachments: Brightlane_Renewal_Summary_v3.pdf (for your records)

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 17:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Brightlane renewal — final approval (conditional)

Thanks for the concise thread. I reviewed the impact and the strategic context. I approve Option A as presented: 10% one-time invoice credit + one-time 60-day service credit + 12-month reset. This approval is conditioned on two items:

1) Legal must sign off on the SLA addendum language; we cannot accept open-ended failure credits.
2) The amendment must include a clause that prices for the 12-month reset do not change (no additional discounting) unless we mutually agree.

Once legal confirms the SLA redline, Jordan: you have my sign-off to execute and route to DocuSign. Please confirm when the amendment is out.

Evelyn Hart
Chief Revenue Officer | Redwood Inference
